exactText: set off inflationary pressures of a kind we have not seen in a generation.
sourceQuote: set off inflationary pressures of a kind we have not seen in a generation.
normalizedClaim: The $1.9 trillion American Rescue Plan will generate inflationary pressures of a magnitude not seen in a generation.
resolutionCriteria: BLS CPI year-over-year inflation rate exceeding 5% (highest in decades) within 12-18 months of the bill’s passage.

resolution.explanation: CPI inflation peaked above 9% YoY in mid-2022, the highest in 40 years.

exactText: the odds are probably better than half that a recession will start next year.
sourceQuote: the odds are probably better than half that a recession will start next year.
normalizedClaim: Probability greater than 50% that a U.S. recession begins in 2023.
resolutionCriteria: NBER Business Cycle Dating Committee declaration of a recession starting in calendar year 2023.

resolution.explanation: No NBER-declared recession began in 2023; the U.S. avoided recession that year.

evidence.sourceTitle: NBER Business Cycle Dating Committee announcements

exactText: We are still headed for a pretty hard landing.
sourceQuote: We are still headed for a pretty hard landing.
normalizedClaim: The U.S. economy is headed for a hard landing (significant rise in unemployment and GDP contraction) as the Fed fights inflation.
resolutionCriteria: NBER recession declaration or unemployment rate rising above 6% combined with two consecutive quarters of negative GDP growth within two years.

resolution.explanation: The U.S. achieved a soft landing; no recession was declared and unemployment remained well below 6%.

exactText: the odds that the economy will go into recession within the next 18 months are quite serious, and probably in the three quarters range.
sourceQuote: the odds that the economy will go into recession within the next 18 months are quite serious, and probably in the three quarters range.
normalizedClaim: Approximately 75% chance of U.S. recession within 18 months (by early 2024).
resolutionCriteria: NBER Business Cycle Dating Committee declaration of recession beginning by February 2024.

resolution.explanation: No NBER recession was declared by early 2024.

exactText: I would expect sometime within the next two or three years, that the unemployment rate will have crossed 6%.
sourceQuote: the unemployment rate will have crossed 6%.
normalizedClaim: U.S. unemployment rate exceeds 6% sometime between 2022 and 2025.
resolutionCriteria: BLS monthly unemployment rate (U-3) reaching or exceeding 6.0% by August 2025.

resolution.explanation: U.S. unemployment rate remained well below 6% throughout the period.

exactText: It's more likely than not that we're going to have a recession—and in the context of a recession, we'll see an extra 2 million people be unemployed.
sourceQuote: It's more likely than not that we're going to have a recession—and in the context of a recession, we'll see an extra 2 million people be unemployed.
normalizedClaim: More likely than not that the U.S. enters a recession (with ~2 million additional unemployed) due to tariff policies.
resolutionCriteria: NBER recession declaration beginning in 2025 or 2026, accompanied by BLS employment data showing approximately 2 million additional unemployed relative to pre-recession levels.

exactText: there was a 60% chance of a 2025 economic recession.
sourceQuote: a 60% chance of a 2025 economic recession.
normalizedClaim: 60% probability of a U.S. recession in calendar year 2025.
resolutionCriteria: NBER Business Cycle Dating Committee declaration of a recession beginning in 2025.

exactText: This is a prescription for the mother of all stagflations.
sourceQuote: This is a prescription for the mother of all stagflations.
normalizedClaim: Implementation of proposed large tariff hikes combined with income-tax cuts will produce severe stagflation (high inflation + stagnant growth).
resolutionCriteria: Simultaneous occurrence of CPI inflation remaining elevated (>4%) and real GDP growth near zero or negative for multiple quarters following significant tariff implementation.

exactText: I think we may be at the foothills of stagflation. I don’t think tariff impacts have been fully felt or will be for some time, and confidence has more room to decline than to rise. I think inflation will surprise a bit on the high side.
sourceQuote: I think we may be at the foothills of stagflation.
normalizedClaim: The U.S. is entering or approaching stagflation, with inflation surprising to the upside due to tariffs.
resolutionCriteria: BLS CPI inflation remaining sticky or rising while real GDP growth slows markedly (near-zero or negative) in subsequent quarters, per BEA data.

exactText: when you have unemployment below 4% and inflation above 4%, recession always follows within two years.
sourceQuote: when you have unemployment below 4% and inflation above 4%, recession always follows within two years.
normalizedClaim: Given 2022 conditions of unemployment <4% and inflation >4%, a U.S. recession will occur within two years (by mid-2024).
resolutionCriteria: NBER recession declaration beginning no later than June 2024.

resolution.explanation: No NBER-declared recession occurred within two years of the 2022 high-inflation/low-unemployment period.
